title: Black & Decker Recalls Random Orbit Sanders Due to Laceration Hazard
summary: The black plastic disc (called the platen) that holds the sandpaper can fly off or break apart during use and the disc, or pieces of the disc, can hit the user or those nearby, posing a laceration hazard. Units: About 192,000.

title: Jo-Ann Fabric and Craft Stores Recalls Roll-Up Blinds due to Risk of Strangulation
summary: Strangulation can occur when the lifting loop slides off the side of the blind and a child's neck becomes entangled on the free-standing loop, or if a child places his/her neck between the lifting loop and the roll-up blind material. Units: About 1,800.

title: Rechargeable Spotlights Recalled by Innovage Due to Burn Hazard
summary: The spotlight's charging adapter can overcharge the battery, forcing it to rupture and leak battery acid. This poses a chemical burn hazard to consumers. Units: About 1.4 Million.

title: Simms Fishing Products Recalls Wading Staffs Due to Fall Hazard
summary: The wading staff can collapse posing a fall hazard to consumers. Units: About 3,000.

title: The Land of Nod Recalls Toy Vegetables Due to Laceration Hazard
summary: The metal wire in the toy asparagus can become exposed, posing a laceration hazard to children. Units: About 2,100.

title: Step2® Recalls Children's Transportation Station Toys Due to Choking Hazard
summary: The light blue plastic wheels on the train cars can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children. Units: About 56,000 in the United States (7,700 in Canada).

title: Subwoofer Speakers Recalled by Paradigm Electronics Due to Fire Hazard
summary: The subwoofer can overheat when the speaker system is played at high outputs for an extended period of time, posing a fire hazard to consumers. Units: About 2,200.

title: Toshiba Recalls T Series Notebook Computers Due to Burn Hazard
summary: The notebook computers can overheat at the notebook's plug-in to the AC adapter, posing a burn hazard to consumers. Units: About 41,000 worldwide.

title: Swing Sets Recalled by Kompan Inc. for Repair Due to Fall Hazard
summary: The joint connection between the horizontal top beam and the vertical end bracket and support post system can crack and break, posing a fall and impact hazard to users. Units: About 700.

title: Molenaar LLC Recalls Night Lights Due to Fire and Shock Hazard
summary: The night lights can become hot to the touch and melt, resulting in risk of possible shock or fire. Units: About 315,000.

title: Rugs Recalled by Brumlow Mills Due to Fire Hazard; Sold Exclusively at J.C. Penney
summary: The large rugs fail to meet federal flammability standards and could ignite, posing the risk of fire and burn hazards to consumers. The small rugs fail to meet federal labeling requirements. summary: The recalled circuit breakers have a spring clip that can break during normal use, leading to a loss of force to maintain a proper electrical connection in the panelboard. title: Children's Mood Rings and Necklaces Recalled by D&D Distributing-Wholesale Due To Risk of Lead Exposure
summary: The metal rings and necklaces contain high levels of lead. Lead is toxic if ingested by young children and can cause adverse health effects. Units: About 19,000 Rings and 4,000 Necklaces.

title: The Gerson Company Recalls Glass Vases Due to Laceration Hazard
summary: The glass vases can break or fracture, posing a laceration hazard to consumers. Units: About 203,000 in the U.S. and 9,000 in Canada.

title: Children's Hooded Jackets and Sweatshirts with Drawstrings Recalled By Burlington Coat Factory Due to Strangulation Hazard
summary: The hooded jackets and sweatshirts have drawstrings through the hood and/or waist which can pose a strangulation or entrapment hazard to children. Units: About 10,000.

title: Tea Sets Recalled by The Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf® Due to Fire Hazard
summary: Sparking from the metallic decorations on the tea sets can result if used in a microwave oven, posing a risk of fire. Units: About 1,600.

title: Chuck E. Cheese’s Recalls Light-up Rings and Star Glasses Due to Ingestion Hazard
summary: If crushed or pulled apart, the plastic casing can break into small pieces and possibly expose the batteries, posing an ingestion hazard to children. If ingested, the batteries may be damaging to either the stomach, intestine, esophagus or nasal mucus membrane. Units: About 1,100,000 Light-up Rings

title: Giant Starbuilders and Giant Stars Building Sets Recalled by Edushape Due to Choking Hazard
summary: Plastic knobs can break from the center of the star, posing a choking hazard to young children. Units: About 13,500.

title: Albee Baby Recalls C & T International/Sorelle Brand "Prescott" Cribs Due to Entrapment, Suffocation and Fall Hazards
summary: These cribs are re-labeled fixed-sided Simplicity cribs that contain tubular metal mattress-support frames recalled in April 2010. title: Fun Stuff Recalls Children's Toys Due to Choking Hazard
summary: The small balls on the end of the toy's arms can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children. The toys were marketed for children age 3 and over. title: Horizon Hobby Recalls Spektrum Receivers Used with Model Airplane Gliders Due to Risk of Injury
summary: The receiver can lose contact with the model airplane glider's radio control while within normal radio range limits. If this happens, the glider can fall from the sky and hit consumers, posing a risk of injury. Units: About 3,500 in the United States and 150 in Canada.

title: The Coleman Company Recalls Water-Activated Spotlights Due to Risk of Impact Injury
summary: The lens assembly can come apart from the main housing of the spotlight with force and pose a risk of impact injuries to consumers. Units: About 50,000 units.

title: Fisher-Price Recalls Children's Trikes Due to Risk of Serious Injury
summary: A child can strike, sit or fall on the protruding plastic ignition key resulting in serious injury, including genital bleeding. Units: About 7 Million in the United States and 150,000 in Canada.

title: Fisher-Price Recalls Healthy Care, Easy Clean and Close to Me High Chairs Due to Laceration Hazard
summary: Children can fall on or against the pegs on the rear legs of the high chair resulting in injuries or lacerations. The pegs are used for high chair tray storage. Units: About 950,000 high chairs in the U.S. and 125,000 in Canada.

title: Fisher-Price Recalls Infant Toys with Inflatable Balls Due to Choking Hazard
summary: The valve of the inflatable ball on these toys can come off and pose a choking hazard to young children. Units: About 2.8 million in the US and about 125,000 in Canada.

title: Fisher-Price Recalls Little People Wheelies Stand 'n Play Rampway Due to Choking Hazard
summary: The wheels on the purple and the green cars can come off, posing a choking hazard to young children. Units: About 100,000 in the U.S. and 20,000 in Canada.

title: Black & Decker Recalls Cordless Electric Lawnmowers Due to Laceration Hazard
summary: The lawnmower's motor and blade can unexpectedly turn on after the mower's safety key is removed, posing a laceration hazard to consumers. title: S T U F F and Paw Wall Hooks Recalled By Midwest-CBK Due to Violation of Lead Paint Standard
summary: Paint on the metal hooks and on the blue paw hook contains excessive levels of lead, violating the federal lead paint standard. Units: 4450.

title: Sunrise Medical Recalls Quickie® Shark Bikes Due to Footrest Failure
summary: The custom footrests can break, posing a risk of injury to the rider. Units: About 20.
